st pope john paul lived through the horrors of nazism and communism. he witnessed what happens when human beings are stripped of their dignity and treated as objects rather than persons. in his encyclical eva ngelium vitae, he warned that when we lose our sense of god, we risk losing our sense of the human person. when we forget that every human being is created in god’s image and likeness, we begin to measure people by their usefulness or co nvenience rather than their inherent dignity. i heard something recently that really struck me: “there was a time when we used things and loved people. today, unfortunately, we seem to love things and use people.” this is a real danger in our increasingly secular society, where the unborn, the elderly and the vulnerable c an be regarded as burdens rather than precious human beings. human dignity is not bestowed by the state or earned through achievement. it comes from god. this is why jesus places love of god first. when we recognise god as our father, we begin to recognise every human being as our brother or sister. whe n we forget god, we risk forgetting what it means to be human. may we as a nation realise the consequences of removing god from our lives. we just simply don’t remove god but we remove the innate dignity of every human person. glenflesk
